title: Zambia Catch Up caregiver attendance-information messaging

user_context.archetype: Zambia education implementer already considering or operating Catch Up
user_context.decision: Whether a caregiver attendance-information messaging add-on should be tested next alongside existing Catch Up, rather than scaled or treated as proven.
user_context.scope: Grade 3-5 Catch Up pupils where child-level school and Catch Up exposure can be measured reliably.

feasible_options.label: TEST
feasible_options.description: Run a small randomized add-on pilot of weekly caregiver information on school and Catch Up attendance.

feasible_options.label: DO NOT TEST
feasible_options.description: Do not run the messaging pilot; preserve resources for other implementation improvements.

feasible_options.label: CANNOT DECIDE
feasible_options.description: Use when local exposure-data capability or incremental pilot cost cannot be established well enough to route the decision.

routing_recommendation.rule: TEST next only if reliable child-level data can cheaply distinguish school absence, present-but-missed Catch Up, Catch Up non-delivery, and Catch Up attendance. Otherwise CANNOT DECIDE pending an exposure-data feasibility and micro-costing check.
not_authorized: claim of superior cost-effectiveness versus standard Catch Up

closest_same_package_research.setting: seven low-income schools in Santiago, Chile
closest_same_package_research.intervention: weekly attendance messages plus monthly grade/behavior messages
closest_same_package_research.use: research denominator only; not a Zambia budget estimate

mechanism_close_african_evidence.result: weekly parent messages reporting after-school-program attendance increased attendance about 5.6%-6.1%
mechanism_close_african_evidence.reported_cost: about R1.01 per child per week
mechanism_close_african_evidence.limitation: no downstream learning outcome; accounting scope is not portable to Zambia

zambia_local_feasibility_evidence.intervention: nine-month parent-facing SMS plus monthly-meeting early-reading package
zambia_local_feasibility_evidence.limitation: different bundled intervention; does not isolate attendance/exposure and is not a cost denominator for attendance messaging

required_zambia_denominators: incremental cost per additional realized Catch Up session
benefits_costs_denominators.cannot_compare: Current evidence cannot defensibly compare caregiver messaging cost-effectiveness with standard Catch Up or other marginal interventions because denominators, packages, settings, and mechanisms are incompatible.

uncertainties_and_contrary_evidence: The closest cost+attendance+learning evidence is from Chile, not Zambia.
Cape Town evidence is mechanism-close but lacks learning outcomes and comes from a master's thesis.
The Zambia SMS evidence changes home reading directly and includes monthly meetings, so it does not identify attendance messaging as the causal mechanism.
Messaging cannot fix Catch Up non-delivery or other non-family-controllable causes of missed exposure.
An attendance gain has limited decision value if it does not increase realized Catch Up sessions or if added exposure does not improve policy-relevant learning.
adoption_constraints: reliable Catch Up session delivery and attendance data
caregiver phone-number matching and message deliverability
SIM churn, language, and caregiver literacy
low incremental data-cleaning and staff burden
adequate Catch Up instructional quality when sessions are attended

toward_do_not_test: exposure states cannot be distinguished cheaply
pilot micro-costing is high relative to plausible exposure gain
messaging cannot target a family-controllable bottleneck
toward_scale_later: randomized Zambia evidence shows meaningful added realized Catch Up exposure
incremental cost per added session is decision-competitive using compatible denominators
effects persist and implementation remains reliable
stop_after_pilot: recorded attendance rises without meaningful added Catch Up exposure
added exposure does not improve policy-relevant learning

highest_value_next_information_request: Before committing to the pilot, obtain a small Zambia Catch Up operational sample showing whether school absence, present-but-missed Catch Up, Catch Up non-delivery, and Catch Up attendance can be distinguished reliably, plus a micro-cost estimate for producing those states and sending/monitoring weekly caregiver messages.

canonical_provenance.role: productization acceptance criteria and user-value test

reduces_search_synthesis_burden.reason: Consolidates route, evidence boundaries, operational constraints, incompatible denominators, and next information request into one decision object.

better_specified_than_literature_summary.reason: Returns a conditional TEST/CANNOT DECIDE routing rule with explicit kill conditions rather than an intervention-effect narrative.

avoids_unsupported_scalar_ranking.reason: Does not rank messaging against Catch Up or other interventions on a common scalar without compatible denominators.

surfaces_uncertainty_noncomparability.reason: Separates pilot plausibility from Zambia effectiveness and scale/cost-effectiveness claims.

reproducible_from_canonical_evidence.reason: All substantive inputs point to integrated canonical P05 synthesis; independent C should challenge fidelity and reproducibility.

identifies_next_information_request.reason: Requests local exposure-state feasibility plus micro-costing because that information directly gates TEST versus CANNOT DECIDE.

decision_delta: Transforms integrated P05 evidence from a research conclusion into an implementer routing rule: conditionally TEST a bounded Zambia caregiver attendance-information add-on only when exposure-state data are feasible; otherwise CANNOT DECIDE. It explicitly rejects scale and cross-intervention cost-effectiveness inference.
review_required: Independent Worker C product-level challenge before Worker D integration
